    Paul Popper/Popperfoto/Popperfoto via Getty Images
    Marie Curie, the Polish physicist and chemist who conducted pioneering research on radioactivity, circa 1920. Curie was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, the first person and only woman to win the Nobel Prize twice and in two different fields, the first woman professor at the University of Paris and the first woman to be entombed on her own merits in the Pantheon in Paris.

    Overview

    Description

    Maria Salomea Skłodowska Curie, better known as Marie Curie, was a Polish and naturalised-French physicist and chemist. She shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics with her husband, Pierre Curie, "for their joint researches on the radioactivity phenomena discovered by Professor Henri Becquerel". Wikipedia
    Born: November 7, 1867, Warsaw, Poland
    Died: July 4, 1934 (age 66 years), Passy, France
    Awards: Nobel Prize in Physics, Nobel Prize in Chemistry · See more
    Spouse: Pierre Curie (m. 1895–1906)
    Education: University of Paris (1903), University of Paris (1894) · See more
    Children: Ève Curie, Irène Joliot-Curie
    Parents: Władysław Skłodowski, Bronisława Skłodowska
